newsitem.title: DENMARK: Peru rebels vow never to give up in hostage drama.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels vow never to give up in hostage drama.

text.p: Peruvian Marxist rebels holding 74 hostages in the Japanese Embassy residence in Lima vowed on Friday never to surrender and appealed to Peru's government to negotiate an end to the month-long standoff.

"We have said it a million times, we will say it again. We will never give in," Isaac Velasco, Hamburg-based international spokesman of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA), said at a news conference in the Danish capital.
MRTA rebels stormed the residence on December 17 to demand the release of some 400 jailed colleagues.
"The crisis will end when the Peruvian government decides it will and when it is willing to make a compromise," he said.

"The MRTA has tried all the time to be flexible and seek a political solution. (Peruvian President) Alberto Fujimori is more concerned about keeping up a strong man image. That is why there is no political solution yet," Velasco added.

On Thursday in Lima, Peruvian government negotiator Domingo Palermo rejected a rebel proposal that the Guatemalan government take part in talks to end the siege and said he had cut off Red Cross and family visits to jailed MRTA members.
Rebel leader Nestor Cerpa Cartolini replied that the government was creating obstacles to solving the crisis and ruled out further hostage releases anytime soon.

In Copenhagen, Velasco said that MRTA wanted Spain or Italy, as well as Guatemala to sit on a "guarantor commission" proposed by the government to oversee talks to end the crisis. Both sides have agreed to the participation of the International Committee of the Red Cross and the Vatican.
